Since he is a state functionary (public official), it's "受贿" (state staff). The examples differentiate "非国家工作人员受贿" for non-state employees. Here he is a public employee, so "受贿". Also possibly "滥用职权" if he used his authority to favor them. In many examples, when both bribery and abuse of power present, they list both: e.g., "受贿;滥用职权". In the case of Jiang case (姜1某) they had both receiving bribes and abusing authority. Here, the facts: He used his position to accept bribes and also provided help to win bids. That's abuse of power. So likely both charges: "受贿" and "滥用职权". The examples: For similar scenario (姜1) they gave both. For others where only bribery is mentioned, they gave only "受贿". Let's see: In the first example (林某某挪用公司货款) they gave "挪用资金". For bribery examples: "非国家工作人员受贿" when not a state employee. For state employee bribery: e.g., "受贿;滥用职权" appears when also abuse. In the case of "沈阳市皇姑区人民检察院指控... 受贿" they gave "受贿;滥用职权". Actually that case had both bribery and abuse of power (receiving bribes and also abusing). So we should output both.

Thus answer: [罪名]受贿;滥用职权<eoa>
